source.title: Increasing Depth Leads to U-Shaped Test Risk in Over-parameterized Convolutional Networks
source.authors: Eshaan Nichani; Adityanarayanan Radhakrishnan; C. Uhler

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own results showing that increasing depth in interpolating convolutional networks can worsen test performance, and that deeper fully convolutional networks approach or can perform worse than a fully connected comparison. This refines the scope of architecture-related generalization claims; it does not test random-label memorization or width scaling.
record.gate_note: The paper's depth sweeps and convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons are its own results. Claims about width scaling and random-label fitting in the Introduction and Related Work are cited prior work and are not rows. Detailed plotted values are figure-only.
record.test_reason: The study tests V3 through its own convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparisons and qualifies the convolutional advantage at large depths. Contrary to the record, Figure 1(a) also reports an original width-scaling result bearing on V2: wider interpolating ResNets have lower test error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors report U-shaped test risk with increasing depth in finite- and infinite-width convolutional networks. Their linear CNTK framework links depth to feature transformations and shows that variance is minimized by inverse-covariance alignment and bias decreases with predictor alignment. Extending this theoretical explanation to nonlinear kernels remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies increasing depth in interpolating CNNs and linear CNTKs, rather than the listed versions' random-label, width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth, width, dataset, class count, padding, pooling versus flattening, and whether training reaches interpolation affect the reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing depth beyond a critical value worsens generalization in interpolating ResNets, Fully-Conv Nets, and nonlinear CNTKs; width-8 ResNets instead plateau without reaching zero training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing convolutional-network depth can produce U-shaped test risk, including beyond interpolation.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear CNTK feature transformations change with depth under zero padding; MNIST regression loss is approximately minimized where the transformation best aligns with the predictor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth-dependent feature transformations can explain U-shaped test risk in linear CNTK regression.

record.problems: Some comparisons and detailed test-risk values are presented only in figures. The main ResNet runs average three seeds; fully convolutional runs use five seeds, with wider-model experiments using three. The width-8 ResNet does not reach zero training loss, limiting its relevance to interpolating behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The many depth-sweep results are relevant to the general claim but do not match a listed version except the fully-convolutional versus fully-connected comparison in V3.

untested.parts: No matched natural-label and random-label training experiments.

The original one-hidden-layer, convergence-trained setting without explicit regularization and behavior around the interpolation threshold are not tested; the reported width comparison uses interpolating ResNets on CIFAR10.
The contribution of local connectivity versus weight sharing, learned sparse connections in fully connected networks, and initialization from trained convolutional networks are not isolated.
No controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; different architectures use different recipes.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: An original width-scaling result: interpolating CIFAR10 ResNets have decreasing test error as width increases. Add rows by fixed depth and width, including training accuracy and test error where readable. The record incorrectly treats width scaling as cited prior work only.
missing.locator: Introduction, Figure 1(a) and its caption; training protocol in Section 3.1

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Numerical curves are unavailable in the supplied text, so qualitative captions and explicit result statements support the verdicts. The pooled worse-than-fully-connected statement cannot establish which individual conditions reverse V3.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not train on random labels or compare natural-label and random-label test performance.
The study varies depth, not width beyond the interpolation threshold.

It compares fully convolutional networks with a wide fully connected network on CIFAR10 and ImageNet32, but does not isolate local connectivity or test sparse learned connections or convolutional initialization.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD generalization comparison is tested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison is tested.
No memorized-example removal experiment is tested.

rows.subject: Fully-Conv Net
rows.operation_detail: Increase depth and compare test accuracy with the wide fully connected network shown in the figures.
rows.measure: Test accuracy relative to the wide fully connected network
rows.baseline: wide fully connected network shown in red
rows.locator: Appendix C, Figures 16 and 19; accompanying text
rows.note: The text says performance approaches that of a wide fully connected network as depth increases; figure values are not given in the supplied text.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison is supported by Figure 16's caption: the convolutional network approaches the fully connected baseline as depth increases. Figure 19 measures cross-entropy loss, not accuracy. The pooled Appendix C statement that performance can become worse does not identify which dataset, class count, or depth exhibits reversal; do not assign reversal to this entire row. Width-16 ten-class models are before or at interpolation, unlike the interpolating two- and five-class settings.
